description: The project-management verbs the Castalie MCP server exposes to your agent. Strictly outward: your assistant reads strategy, briefs and specs and writes back statuses, plans and follow-ups. No verb accepts source code, a diff, or file content — Castalie never sees your repository. And no verb sends anything out of your tenant but one: kit_feedback_send, which sends to the team that publishes the kit, on a person's yes, an improvement to the kit itself — the kit file, the diagnosis, the change proposed to the kit, the kit version. Never your code, your files or your data. Everything else written here stays in your own instance. Support is blind by construction — nothing in this contract can change that, and no skill asks a user to.

transport.url: https://<your-workspace>.castalie.app/mcp (every workspace answers on its own host; registered per project by the setup command, never hardcoded)
transport.auth: Bearer token in the Authorization header (posted by the setup command); token is looked up by its SHA-256, so it never travels or is stored in clear on the server

workflow_options.description: The complete vocabulary of workflow preferences this kit knows: which skill owns which option, and the canonical values each accepts. This is the single authority - the enums on workflow_default_set, workflow_default_unset and workflow_policy_resolve are checked against it, and so is every option a skill cites. An option that is not here does not exist.
workflow_options.server_owned_note: Namespaces in the vocabulary below that NO skill of this kit owns: the Castalie instance itself honours them, and the agent's only business with them is setting them. They are listed so that the 'declared but never read' check does not cry ghost over an option the product really does read - and a name here that IS one of this kit's skills is refused, so the exemption cannot be used to silence a real ghost.

rest_api.description: The REST surface the `cs` CLI uses (Castalie's PmContentController), same Bearer auth. Read side only + the markdown body round-trip. Content bodies are raw markdown whose sections are delimited by <!-- @field <name> --> and composed/parsed server-side.

routes.returns: text/markdown (fields: brief = executive/problem/vision/hors-scope, spec = executive/problem/solution, bug = description/technical-detail)

routes.note: a field absent from the submitted markdown is left unchanged; type = feature-brief | feature-spec | bug. A bug section is written only when it changes, by the same rule as bug_update_field, and its history keeps the value it replaced

conventions.return_envelope: Every tool returns a JSON string { success: bool, ... } and { success: false, error: string } on failure.
conventions.bodies: Long markdown bodies (brief problem/vision, spec executive summary/problem/solution, ticket description/technical detail) are never passed as tool arguments — read and write them with the `cs content pull|push <type> <id>` CLI. Tools carry metadata only (title, phases, status, risks).
conventions.forbidden_fields: No tool declares a parameter named code, diff, patch, file_content or source_code. The flow is outward-only.
conventions.addresses: An entity answer MAY carry `url`, the absolute https address of that entity's own page, computed by the workspace that served it because it alone knows its host: on `feature_spec_get` and `feature_brief_get`, on each node of `strategy_get_objective_breadcrumb`, on each item of `strategy_navigate_children`, and on any objective a workspace answers outside this contract. It is optional in both directions — a workspace that serves none is conformant, and a client that reads it falls back to plain text when it is absent, and when it is an address its own surface would refuse.

tools.name: whoami
tools.description: Identify the authenticated Castalie user and workspace for this session (resolved from the token, no parameter). Use it for the user_id that feature_spec_pick and other per-user tools expect — and for the workspace mark, which callers outside a browser have no other way to learn: logo_url and accent_color are null when the workspace has declared none, meaning "use the product's own mark", never "use none".

tools.name: strategy_list_periods
tools.description: List all strategy periods (annual, quarterly).

params.name: periodType
params.description: Filter: 'annual' or 'quarterly'.

returns.periods: [{ id, name, period_type, start_date, end_date, parent_period_id, parent_period_name, child_count }]

tools.name: strategy_navigate_children
tools.description: Drill down one level (or up to depth=3) inside the objectives tree without loading the whole strategy. Pass periodId for the period's root objectives, OR objectiveId for that objective's children. Mutually exclusive.

params.name: periodId
params.description: List the period's root objectives. Required if objectiveId is omitted.

params.name: objectiveId
params.description: List this objective's direct children. Required if periodId is omitted.

params.name: depth
params.description: Levels to expand: 1..3 (hard cap).

params.name: includeKrs
params.description: Include key results per objective.

returns.items: [{ id, title, icon, objective_type, parent_objective_id, is_linked, computed_progress, child_count, has_children, key_result_count, key_results?, url? }]

tools.name: strategy_search_objectives
tools.description: Search objectives by title. Use it when the user names an objective but you have no id; prefer strategy_navigate_children once you have an anchor.

params.name: q
params.description: Search term matched against objective titles.

tools.name: strategy_create_objective
tools.description: Create a strategy objective, at the root of a period or under a parent. The audit uses it to give its work a home when the team has none yet — and asks before calling it: an objective is the team's strategy, not the audit's own output.

params.name: title
params.description: Objective title, in the user's language.

params.name: period_id
params.description: Period it belongs to. Defaults to the current one.

params.name: parent_objective_id
params.description: Parent objective. Null for a root objective — this is what makes a sub-objective a single call.

tools.name: strategy_get_objective_breadcrumb
tools.description: Return the parent chain of an objective from root to leaf, one node per level. Use it to build the objective header of a spec without loading the whole strategy.

params.name: objectiveId
params.description: Objective whose ancestor chain we want.

params.name: includeVision
params.description: Include the top ambition/vision tier. Default false (stop at the annual root).

returns.chain: [{ id, title, icon, objective_type, period_id, period_name, url? }]

tools.name: strategy_my_okrs
tools.description: The objectives someone is accountable for, with their key results, their progress and the LAST CHECK-IN of each. One call for 'where do my key results stand?', and the same selection the 'My OKRs' screen shows, so an agent and the page cannot answer differently. Every key result carries days_since_check_in: a figure at 40% reads the same whether it was reported yesterday or never, and that is what tells the two apart.

params.name: owner_user_id
params.description: Whose objectives. Defaults to the authenticated user.

params.name: period_id
params.description: Which period. Left out, the latest one.

params.name: team_id
params.description: A whole team's load instead of one person's. A team wins over the user.

returns.objectives: [{ objective, parent_title, key_results: [{ id, title, unit, start_value, target_value, current_value, computed_progress, last_check_in, days_since_check_in, report_id?, report_table_id?, external_report_url? }] }]

tools.name: strategy_check_in_history
tools.description: The recorded check-ins of one key result, most recent first, each with who reported it. Answers 'is this figure really moving?', which the value of the day cannot.

params.name: take
params.description: How many, most recent first (1..100).

returns.check_ins: [{ id, previous_value, new_value, confidence, comment, author_user_id, author_name, date_created }]

tools.name: strategy_get_objective
tools.description: One objective read by its id, with its key results — each carrying its latest check-in and how many days old that figure is — its owner, its team, the title of its parent, and main_key_result_id when one is designated. An archived objective reads as absent (objective_not_found).

returns.key_results: [{ id, title, metric_type, unit, start_value, target_value, current_value, computed_progress, last_check_in, days_since_check_in, report_id?, report_table_id?, external_report_url? }]

tools.name: strategy_create_check_in
tools.description: Record where a key result stands today: the value, the confidence and one sentence. This is the normal way to move a figure — it leaves a dated trace and refreshes every gauge above it. The author is resolved from the token, so a check-in is always signed.

params.name: new_value
params.description: The value today. It comes from the user, never from a deduction.

params.name: confidence
params.description: on_track | at_risk | off_track — the owner's reading, not the agent's.

params.name: comment
params.description: What explains the figure, in one or two sentences.

tools.name: strategy_create_key_result
tools.description: Add a key result to an objective. A key result is what makes the objective measurable, and it is read off a report: pass report_id (a report of this workspace, computed by the engine) or external_report_url (a report elsewhere, computed by nothing) so it is born linked. A refused link creates nothing. The value arrives at the first calculation: call strategy_refresh_key_result right after creating with report_id.

params.name: objective_id
params.description: Objective this key result measures.

params.name: title
params.description: What is measured, in the user's language.

params.name: metric_type
params.description: number | percent | currency | boolean. Anything else becomes number.

params.name: unit
params.description: Unit shown next to the figure (€, %, clients).

params.name: start_value
params.description: Value it starts from.

params.name: target_value
params.description: Value to reach.

params.name: current_value
params.description: Value today. Defaults to the starting value.

params.name: previous_value_type
params.description: period_start (progress along the way, the default) | previous_period (a historical marker, the counter restarts at zero for this period).

params.name: report_id
params.description: A report of THIS workspace that measures the key result: its value is the first cell of the report's first active table, its curve the second table. Must be an active main report the caller may read; refused otherwise (report_forbidden, report_not_found, reports_unavailable), and nothing is created.

params.name: report_table_id
params.description: One table of that report to read the value from instead of its first one. Must belong to the report (report_table_not_in_report).

params.name: external_report_url
params.description: HTTPS address of a report that lives in ANOTHER system. A reader can open it; nothing is computed from it. Anything but https is refused (external_report_url_https_required). The address of a report of this workspace is read as its report_id.

tools.name: strategy_update_key_result
tools.description: Correct a key result's definition — title, unit, starting value, target — fix a current value entered by mistake, or link it to the report its value is read from. A figure that has genuinely MOVED is recorded with strategy_create_check_in instead, which leaves the trace. Only the fields passed are changed; a unit left out is kept.

params.name: metric_type
params.description: number | percent | currency | boolean

params.name: current_value
params.description: A correction, not a move. To move it, use strategy_create_check_in.

params.name: objective_id
params.description: Attach it to another objective.

params.name: previous_value_type
params.description: period_start | previous_period.

params.name: report_id
params.description: A report of THIS workspace that measures the key result: the engine reads its value from the first cell of the report's first active table, and its curve from the second table — every day, and on strategy_refresh_key_result. Pass 0 to unlink. Must be an active main report the caller may read; refused otherwise, and a refusal leaves the whole call untouched.

params.name: report_table_id
params.description: One table of the linked report to read the value from instead of its first one. Pass 0 to go back to the first table. Must belong to the linked report.

params.name: external_report_url
params.description: HTTPS address of a report that lives in ANOTHER system. A reader can open it; nothing is computed from it. Pass an empty string to remove it. Anything but https is refused (external_report_url_https_required).

tools.name: strategy_refresh_key_result
tools.description: Recalculate a key result from the report of this workspace it is linked to (report_id), as the sheet's « Recalculer maintenant » does: the value is read from the report as the caller would read it, becomes the current value and today's point in its history. No check-in is written. Refused with no_automatic_value when the key result has no report of this workspace, or when the report cannot be read — the message says which.

tools.name: report_get_context
tools.description: The report-building rules of this workspace — where the SQL runs, column formats, graphic types — and the schema a report may read. Served only where the workspace has reports, to those allowed to author them. Read it before report_create and report_save_table.

returns.(text): the authoring rules and the readable schema

tools.name: report_create
tools.description: Create an empty report of this workspace, attached to the work it measures: featureSpecId for one spec, featureBriefId for a whole feature. Its page is /Report/Viewer/View/{reportId} on the workspace host. The report_* authoring verbs are the report owner's.

params.name: featureSpecId
params.description: The spec it measures.

params.name: featureBriefId
params.description: The feature it measures as a whole.

tools.name: report_save_table
tools.description: Create or update one table of a report: its SQL, its columns and its options (graphic_type, sub_title…). The SQL is a read, run under the workspace's read-only report account. Call report_get_context first.

params.name: sql
params.description: A SELECT (or WITH) over the workspace's readable schema.

params.name: columns
params.description: JSON array: [{ index, title, align?, format?, … }] — one per SELECT column.

params.name: tableId
params.description: Existing table to update; omitted, a new one is created.

params.name: parameters
params.description: JSON array of SQL parameter definitions.

params.name: options
params.description: JSON: { has_total?, has_average?, graphic_type?, sub_title?, description? }.

tools.name: report_read_table
tools.description: Read a report of this workspace the way its page shows it, computed by the same engine. Open to every member. Pass report_id alone to list its readable tables; pass report_table_id to read one table's columns and rows. Refusals: forbidden, reports_unavailable (this workspace serves no report), not_found, sql_error, invalid_parameters, missing_target.

params.name: parameters
params.description: JSON object of parameter name to value.

tools.name: feature_brief_create
tools.description: Create a new feature brief (business framing: title, domain, objective). Returns the new brief id. Write the body (problem/vision/executive summary) with `cs content push feature-brief <id>`, not as arguments.

params.name: domain
params.description: marketing | product | internal | editorial

params.name: ownerUserId
params.description: Served as owner_user_id. Who the brief belongs to: the person who asked for it, or the workspace's automation account, named without their token (instructions/on-whose-behalf.md). Must be an active member, otherwise owner_not_found and nothing is created. The author stays the caller.

params.name: nextFollowupDate
params.description: ISO YYYY-MM-DD.

tools.name: feature_single_deliverable_create
tools.description: ONE deliverable, one pull request: creates a brief, its single user story and a spec with one phase, in a single gesture. Use it when the work is one thing that takes an afternoon — not a need with several stories, which is feature_brief_create, and not something broken, which is bug_create. Filing small work through the brief door asks for a problem, a vision, an out-of-scope and a phased plan, and what happens is not that people write all of it: it is that they write none of it. The brief is created Accepted, because somebody who names one deliverable has already decided it is worth doing.

params.name: title
params.description: What is being delivered, in one line. It titles the brief, the spec and the phase.

params.name: persona
params.description: Persona (who). Supply the three story fields or none.

params.name: action
params.description: Action (wants to).

params.name: benefit
params.description: Benefit (so that).

params.name: problem_md
params.description: What is wrong or missing today (markdown). Carried by both the brief and the spec.

params.name: solution_md
params.description: How it will be done (markdown). Carried by the spec and by its single phase.

params.name: objective_id
params.description: Optional strategy objective to attach.

params.name: owner_user_id
params.description: Who the deliverable is for: the person who asked for it, or the workspace's automation account, named without their token (instructions/on-whose-behalf.md). Owns the new brief and leads the spec; on an existing brief it only leads the spec. Must be an active member, otherwise owner_not_found and nothing is created. Omit to leave the brief without an owner and the spec without a lead.

tools.name: feature_brief_get
tools.description: Get a feature brief by id, with linked objectives, child specs, owner/team names — its user stories (each with `spec_ids`, the specs that deliver it), its acceptance criteria with their verdicts, and `acceptance`: `can_enter_acceptance`, `can_be_done`, the `missing_items` that stand in the way of Done, and the brief's acceptance pass.

returns.brief: object — may carry `url`, the address of the brief's own page (see conventions.addresses)

tools.name: feature_brief_list
tools.description: List feature briefs with optional filters (period, owner, status, domain, keyword, date windows). Metadata only — no body.

params.name: statusFilter
params.description: Draft | Accepted | InProgress | Done | Canceled

params.name: query
params.description: Keyword search (title + body, case-insensitive).

params.name: take
params.description: Max 150.

tools.name: feature_brief_update
tools.description: Update brief metadata (title/domain/status/priority/objective/nextFollowup). Pass null to leave a field unchanged. For the body, use the content CLI.

params.name: status
params.description: Draft, Accepted, InProgress, Acceptance, Done or Canceled. Castalie moves a brief to Acceptance itself when its last active spec closes with one delivered; Done is refused until the acceptance is conforming and recorded — use feature_brief_accept.

tools.name: feature_brief_add_user_story
tools.description: Add a business user story to a brief (persona / action / benefit). A brief carries no implementation effort.

tools.name: feature_brief_acceptance_pick
tools.description: Claim a brief's acceptance for this machine, so two sessions never replay the same brief. Granted when the brief is in Acceptance and unclaimed, already claimed by the same hostname, or claimed more than 24 hours ago.

returns.reason: string — not_in_acceptance, held_by_another (when claimed is false)

tools.name: feature_brief_acceptance_pick_next
tools.description: Claim the oldest free brief in Acceptance, one per owner per night (from 18:00 UTC).

returns.reason: string — nothing_to_claim, budget_exceeded (when claimed is false)

tools.name: feature_brief_acceptance_release
tools.description: Give a brief's acceptance claim back.

tools.name: feature_brief_set_acceptance_test_status
tools.description: Write the verdict of one of the brief's acceptance criteria: Pass, Fail, NotApplicable, or NotChecked to clear it. Pass and Fail need resultMd — what was done and what was seen; NotApplicable needs the reason.

tools.name: feature_brief_accept
tools.description: Record a conforming acceptance and close the brief (Done) in one call. Refused, and nothing written, unless every active spec is closed with one delivered, every user story is Done or Canceled, every criterion is Pass or NotApplicable, and no acceptance pass is open; the error names what is missing.

tools.name: feature_brief_update_user_story
tools.description: Update the supplied fields of a user story, including its status. Canceled is refused without canceledReason.

tools.name: feature_spec_create
tools.description: Create a technical spec under a brief (1..N specs per brief). Write the body with `cs content push feature-spec <id>`, not as arguments.

params.name: scope
params.description: front | back | batch | mcp | full

tools.name: feature_spec_get
tools.description: Get a spec by id, with phases, risks, acceptance tests, lead name.

returns.spec: object — may carry `url`, the address of the spec's own page (see conventions.addresses)

tools.name: feature_spec_list
tools.description: List specs with optional filters (brief, status, lead, keyword, date windows). Metadata only — no body, no nested phases/risks.

params.name: take
params.description: Max 150.

tools.name: feature_spec_pick
tools.description: Atomically claim a spec for a user (lead = user, status = InProgress). success=false if already claimed by another user.

params.name: userId
params.description: Served as lead_user_id. The lead: the person the work is done for, or the workspace's automation account, named without their token (instructions/on-whose-behalf.md). Must be an active member, otherwise lead_not_found and nothing changes. Omit to default to the authenticated user.

tools.name: feature_spec_update
tools.description: Update spec metadata (title/scope/category/status/priority/estimates) or reassign to another brief. Pass null to leave a field unchanged. For the body, use the content CLI.

params.name: status
params.description: NotStarted | InProgress | Review | Done | Canceled

tools.name: feature_spec_complete
tools.description: Mark a whole spec Done (status = Done, done_at = now). Optionally store the URL of the delivered change (e.g. your PR).

params.name: prUrl
params.description: URL of the delivered change on your side (optional).

tools.name: feature_spec_link_user_story
tools.description: Say that this spec delivers a user story of ITS OWN brief. Castalie closes the story when every active spec linked to it is Done, and reopens it when one of them leaves Done. A story of another brief is refused; linking twice is harmless.

tools.name: feature_spec_unlink_user_story
tools.description: Withdraw the link between a spec and a user story.

tools.name: feature_spec_add_phase
tools.description: Add an implementation phase to a spec (title + plan + estimate). Only objectiveMd is displayed on the sheet; actionPlanMd and validationCriterionMd are read by agents only (instructions/rich-content.md).

tools.name: feature_spec_update_phase
tools.description: Edit an existing phase (amend/correct after creation). Pass null to leave a field unchanged; empty string clears a markdown field. Use feature_spec_set_phase_status for status. Only objectiveMd is displayed on the sheet; actionPlanMd and validationCriterionMd are read by agents only (instructions/rich-content.md).

tools.name: feature_spec_set_phase_status
tools.description: Mark a phase NotStarted | InProgress | Done. A delivery URL is stored when Done.

params.name: status
params.description: NotStarted | InProgress | Done

params.name: prUrl
params.description: Delivery URL, used when status=Done.

tools.name: feature_spec_add_risk
tools.description: Add a typed risk to a spec (Technical|Business|Timeline + severity + probability + mitigation).

params.name: riskType
params.description: Technical | Business | Timeline

params.name: severity
params.description: low | medium | high | critical | mitigated

params.name: probability
params.description: low | medium | high

tools.name: feature_spec_add_acceptance_test
tools.description: Add a technical acceptance test — your assistant verifies it at end of dev. Kind visual|nonvisual; verificationMd holds the URL/command/query to run (no source code).

params.name: kind
params.description: visual | nonvisual

params.name: verificationMd
params.description: How to verify: a URL to open, a command to run, a query to check.

tools.name: feature_spec_update_acceptance_test
tools.description: Edit an existing tech acceptance test (kind, label, verification). Pass null to leave a field unchanged; empty string clears verification.

tools.name: workflow_catalog_list
tools.description: List the workflow options THIS instance actually knows: skill, option, accepted values, and the value that applies when nobody has decided. Read it instead of hardcoding option names - an option this instance does not know is a setting nothing will ever honour, and a value it does not accept is one it will refuse to store. It is also what closes the loop on this contract: the vocabulary declared here is compared to the one the instance serves, so a drift on either side is caught instead of being discovered by a user toggling a control that changes nothing.

tools.name: workflow_policy_resolve
tools.description: Collapse the workspace policy and the user's preference for one skill+option into a single answer, and say who decided. The administrator's policy (allow | deny | user_choice) outranks the user's value; a skill must call this before offering any choice, or it offers a control the user may not have. An unreadable policy is never permission.

params.name: skill
params.description: Skill name without the leading slash.

params.name: option
params.description: Option name. Must belong to the skill named above - see workflow_options.

returns.settings_url: string (the page on the user's Castalie account where both layers are visible)

tools.name: workflow_default_get_all
tools.description: Return every workflow preference stored for the current user, as {skill, option, value}. Skills read this once at the start of a run; empty means use the skill's built-in default.

tools.name: workflow_default_set
tools.description: Persist (upsert) one workflow preference for the current user. value is the canonical machine string the skill expects (e.g. 'stop-before-merge', 'always-manual', 'ask'), always one of the option's own values - 'on' and 'off' are not among them, and never a scalar: the vocabulary is closed and every value in it is a string.

params.name: skill
params.description: Skill name without the leading slash.

params.name: option
params.description: Option key. Must belong to the skill named above - see workflow_options.

params.name: value
params.description: Canonical machine value accepted by that option - see workflow_options. Never a localized label. The instance refuses a value it does not accept for an option it knows, so read workflow_catalog_list rather than guess.

tools.name: workflow_default_unset
tools.description: Remove one workflow preference so the skill falls back to its built-in default.

tools.name: followup_check_add
tools.description: Add a post-delivery follow-up check to a spec (check_type=technical) OR a brief (check_type=business) — exactly one parent. followupPromptMd holds the executable instructions + explicit pass/fail thresholds, written upfront and human-reviewed.

params.name: checkType
params.description: technical | business

params.name: followupPromptMd
params.description: Instructions + pass/fail thresholds (markdown).

params.name: scheduleOffsetDays
params.description: First run at delivered_at + N days.

params.name: featureSpecId
params.description: Technical check — pass this OR featureBriefId, never both.

params.name: featureBriefId
params.description: Business check — pass this OR featureSpecId, never both.

params.name: chainOffsetDays
params.description: Next horizon materialized on pass (null = no chain).

params.name: onFailAction
params.description: bug_fix | implement_spec | create_spec

params.name: anchorPrUrl
params.description: The pull request this check verifies: it then counts from that PR's recorded production delivery, whatever the state of its subject.

params.name: anchorAlias
params.description: With anchorPrUrl, the deployed component whose delivery counts (default: the PR's first delivery).

tools.name: followup_check_list
tools.description: List active follow-up checks for a spec or a brief (ordered by display order).

tools.name: followup_check_update
tools.description: Edit an existing follow-up check. Pass null to leave a field unchanged; empty string clears the prompt. Set isActive=false to deactivate.

params.name: anchorPrUrl
params.description: Anchor the check on its pull request's production delivery; empty string removes the anchor.

tools.name: followup_run_complete
tools.description: Close a follow-up run with its verdict and the evidence seen. On a failure or a decision to take, relaunchPromptMd is handed word for word to the session that takes the work back.

params.name: outcome
params.description: passed | failed | skipped

params.name: notesMd
params.description: What was checked and what it gave.

params.name: finalStatus
params.description: done | failed | human_required

params.name: relaunchPromptMd
params.description: Why the check relaunches the work, what was measured, what to do.

tools.name: acceptance_open
tools.description: Open an acceptance pass on a running feature — one pass = one branch = one pull request. Idempotent on the branch: called again it hands back the pass already open, so a session that crashed and came back does not fork the queue in two. STAYS IN YOUR WORKSPACE, like every verb here.

params.name: title
params.description: What is being reviewed, in the reviewer's own words — not a date and not a branch name.

params.name: branch_name
params.description: The single branch this pass commits to.

tools.name: acceptance_add_remark
tools.description: Add one remark to the queue. Persisted immediately as queued, at the back. Returns at once — never blocks, never waits for the remark to be dealt with, because the person firing remarks is looking at the product and not at a terminal. Carries the remark only: no code, no diff, no file content.

params.name: title
params.description: The remark, as short as it was said.

params.name: description_md
params.description: Any detail worth keeping.

tools.name: acceptance_list
tools.description: Without session_id: the acceptance passes, open ones first. With session_id: that pass's remarks, in the order they were received.

params.name: session_id
params.description: List this pass's remarks instead of the passes.

params.name: status
params.description: queued | in_progress | awaiting_user | done | wont_fix | failed

tools.name: acceptance_claim_next
tools.description: Take the oldest remark waiting, or one whose lease has run out, and hold it under a new lease. Steps over remarks parked on a question — the queue must not stall behind a decision that belongs to a person. Returns claimed=false when there is nothing to do.

params.name: claimed_by
params.description: Who is taking it — a hostname, a session name.

params.name: lease_minutes
params.description: Minutes before the claim expires and the remark can be taken by someone else (default 15).

tools.name: acceptance_resolve
tools.description: Close a remark. done, with the commit that fixed it. wont_fix when it was looked at and deliberately left alone — put the reason in result_md, because what you fixed is readable in the commits and what you knowingly chose NOT to fix is readable nowhere else. failed when it genuinely could not be fixed, reason in result_md too.

params.name: status
params.description: done | wont_fix | failed (default done)

params.name: result_md
params.description: What changed — or why it was left alone.

tools.name: acceptance_park
tools.description: Park a remark on a question only a person can answer. The caller must then move on to the next remark, never wait. Use this only when the answer truly requires a person — anything settleable from the code in under a minute is settled on the spot.

params.name: question_md
params.description: The question, written to be read by the person answering.

tools.name: acceptance_answer
tools.description: Answer a parked question. The remark goes back to the queue at its own place, not at the front: the order the person gave still holds, and an answer is not a reason to jump the line.

tools.name: acceptance_set_pr
tools.description: Attach the pass's single pull request. One pass, one PR: a PR per remark buries the reviewer, and a reviewer who skims is a reviewer you no longer have.

tools.name: acceptance_close
tools.description: Close the pass. merged | abandoned (default merged).

params.name: status
params.description: merged | abandoned

tools.name: onboarding_retro_record
tools.description: Record the retrospective of an onboarding pass - what worked, what rubbed, the open questions, the suggestions - about the PROCESS, not about the team's work. It is written to the client's own tenant and stays there; no policy guards it, because writing in your own workspace asks nobody's permission. The four fields carry process feedback only: never code, file excerpts, paths, host names, command output, secrets, customer or product names, nor any recorded observation. The server redacts as a net and says so; a redaction that fires means something was written that should not have been. STAYS IN YOUR WORKSPACE, like every verb in this contract but kit_feedback_send. Whether the instance forwards anything to Castalie is an instance setting the client's administrator holds, disabled by default - no verb here decides it, and no user is asked.

params.name: run_id
params.description: The maturity run this pass opened.

params.name: worked_md
params.description: What genuinely helped, about the process.

params.name: friction_md
params.description: Where the pass stalled, asked a bad question, or wasted time.

params.name: questions_md
params.description: What the pass could not answer and should have been able to.

params.name: suggestions_md
params.description: What would have made it better, in the user's own words where they gave them.

tools.name: retro_suggestion_add
tools.description: Post an end-of-run retrospective suggestion (status pending) — a durable learning about how the assistant should work. Targets the plugin's own skills or your CLAUDE.md, never your product code. The summary is the lesson + the rule to encode. STAYS IN YOUR WORKSPACE. An improvement to the kit ITSELF goes to kit_feedback_send instead, after a person's yes. Pick between the two retrospective verbs by SUBJECT, not by destination: a learning about YOUR work belongs here; feedback about the ONBOARDING PROCESS belongs to onboarding_retro_record. Neither leaves your tenant.

params.name: source
params.description: Originating skill, e.g. feature_implement | ship | feature_followup

params.name: target_kind
params.description: instruction | skill | command | doc

params.name: target_file
params.description: Path of the file the rule should live in (a pointer, not its content).

params.name: summary
params.description: The lesson + the rule to encode.

tools.name: kit_feedback_send
tools.description: Send an improvement to the Castalie kit ITSELF — a skill, instruction, agent, hook or contract under cs/ — to the team that publishes the kit. The ONE verb that leaves your tenant, and only after a person answered yes to a line showing what leaves: the kit file, the diagnosis, the change proposed to the kit, the kit version. Never your code, your files or your data: proposed_diff may only name paths under cs/ (diff_outside_kit) and is capped at 64 KiB. Keeps a local copy (a retro suggestion, target_kind kit) and returns it with upstream_id once delivered. kit_feedback_disabled: this instance sends nothing, keep the suggestion local with retro_suggestion_add. kit_feedback_send_failed: the copy is kept, call again with its id to resend it without a duplicate. Owner or member only.

params.name: target_file
params.description: Path of the kit file concerned, under cs/. Required unless id is given.

params.name: title
params.description: One-line diagnosis. Required unless id is given.

params.name: summary
params.description: What went wrong and the rule the kit should encode. Required unless id is given.

params.name: proposed_diff
params.description: The change proposed to the kit — paths under cs/ only, never the workspace's files.

params.name: kit_version
params.description: The running kit version, as `cs version` prints it. Required unless id is given.

params.name: id
params.description: Resend a local copy that did not reach the publisher.

tools.name: kit_feedback_status
tools.description: Read back the publisher's decision on a kit improvement sent with kit_feedback_send, and update the local copy: status (pending, accepted, rejected or applied), decision_reason, and pr_url once applied. Owner or member only.

params.name: id
params.description: The local copy's id, as kit_feedback_send returned it.

tools.name: maturity_challenge
tools.description: Read where the team's agent-assisted engineering practices stand: level reached, the single next step, what is at risk, and the criteria nobody has ever looked at.

returns.next_step: { criterion, name, power, guard, unlocks } | null
returns.criteria: [{ criterion, name, level, state (never_probed|observed|stale|partial|absent|unverifiable), unguarded_power, observed_at, expires_at }]
returns.page_url: string (the maturity page — give it, never build one)

tools.name: maturity_start_run
tools.description: Open a maturity pass. Every observation belongs to one.

params.name: kind
params.description: onboarding (the first pass at a new client) | scheduled | manual. Default: manual.

tools.name: maturity_run_probes
tools.description: Run the probes the instance can run on its own — no agent judgement involved. Whatever it cannot see from there is written down as not verifiable, with the reason and who could observe it. Call it before maturity_challenge to work from measured ground rather than from memory.

params.name: kind
params.description: onboarding | scheduled | manual. Default: scheduled.

params.name: run_id
params.description: Run id from maturity_start_run. Omit it and the probes open a run of their own — a second pass on the page, for the same afternoon.

returns.opened_a_new_run: bool (true when the run asked for was not found and a fresh one was opened)

tools.name: maturity_remediation_get
tools.description: The written procedure for putting ONE criterion in place — this product's own method, served by the instance. There is no command per criterion and there never will be: twenty criteria would be twenty entries in a menu nobody reads. Fetch it only for a criterion you are about to work on, and only after the user has asked — a red criterion is not consent. Because it comes from the instance, it is the current method even when the caller's plugin is old. A criterion whose procedure is not written yet answers has_procedure:false — say so, and NEVER write one from memory.

params.name: criterion_id
params.description: Criterion key.

returns.name: string (absent when has_procedure is false)
returns.guard: string (the rule the procedure serves — absent when has_procedure is false)
returns.written_for: string[] (the criteria that DO have one — only when has_procedure is false)

tools.name: maturity_record
tools.description: Record what you OBSERVED for one criterion — never what you assume. Evidence is mandatory except for unverifiable, which needs a reason instead. Never put a secret in the evidence: count and locate, never quote. Read the state it answers with: an unguarded power is stored lower than the state asked for.

params.name: criterion_id
params.description: Criterion key.

params.name: state
params.description: observed | partial | absent | unverifiable

params.name: run_id
params.description: Run id from maturity_start_run.

params.name: evidence_md
params.description: What you saw, in plain words: counts, dates, paths. Never a secret value.

params.name: unverifiable_reason
params.description: Why you could not check it. Required when state is unverifiable.

params.name: unguarded_power
params.description: True when the power exists but you did NOT observe its guard. Forces the state down: an unguarded power never shows green.

returns.state: string (the state actually STORED, which may be lower than the one requested)

tools.name: arbitration_ask
tools.description: Deposit an arbitration you cannot settle yourself, then carry on with everything that does not depend on the answer. Returns the request id, or a refusal saying what to fix.

params.name: title
params.description: The arbitration to settle, not the topic.

params.name: escalation_reason
params.description: money, public_voice, shareholder, private_knowledge or irreversible. If none fits, the arbitration is yours.

params.name: resume_state
params.description: What you need to resume later; never shown to the human.

params.name: answer_shape
params.description: closed (yes / no / other) or open (two or three written options).

params.name: options
params.description: For an open question: title, body, favours, givesUp.

tools.name: arbitration_check
tools.description: Read one arbitration request you deposited: whether it was answered, the answer, and the state you left yourself to resume from.
